What if some of those old poettic eddas had merit in truth? What if Thor and Loki and everyone in Asgard had their memories wiped and there was actually a giant wolf, an eight-legged horse, a giant sea serpent, and a goddess of death directly spawned from Loki? What if Angrboda was actually a monster who took advantage of a much younger Loki?  What if all of this somehow was integrated into the MCU???

title: Frostbound Heart
author: Scarletlatte
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
A treaty between kingdoms shackles you to the one person you cannot stand: Loki.Arrogant, sharp tongued, and impossible to read, Loki has spent years turning every encounter between you into a battlefield. Now, bound by royal decree and trapped beneath the glittering weight of the Asgardian court, the two of you are forced into a marriage neither of you wanted.
The arrangement is simple: survive the arranged marriage, preserve the alliance, and avoid killing each other in the process.But hatred is a dangerous thing when it lingers too long. Especially when it begins to sound like devotion.Between venomous stares, political games, midnight arguments, and a growing tension neither of you dares name, the line between resentment and desire slowly begins to blur, until every glance feels like a challenge, every touch feels catastrophic, and every cruel word hides something far more dangerous beneath it.Because hearts, unlike kingdoms, cannot be ruled by duty alone.

title: Stars Scattered Across a Haunted Galaxy
author: Caligula_Enthusiast
summary:
Kvasir, Następczyni Tronu Alfheimu, znika bez śladu podczas jednej ze swoich wypraw na granice królestwa. Dwór ukrywa jej zaginięcie, obawiając się politycznego chaosu i konfliktu między sojusznikami.
Loki otrzymuje od Rodziny Królewskiej tajną misję odnalezienia księżniczki, zanim jej zniknięcie stanie się początkiem kryzysu, którego nie da się powstrzymać. Jego jedyną pomocą jest Sigyn — jego najbliższa przyjaciółka, wychowana przez ród Ubbego ljosalfarka, która zna stare szlaki, zapomniane miejsca i tajemnice Alfheimu lepiej niż większość mieszkańców królestwa.
Ślad Kvasir prowadzi ich do Járnviðr, miejsca pełnego dawnych sekretów i niebezpiecznej magii. Jednak poszukiwania ujawniają coś znacznie większego — tajemniczą epidemię, która zaczyna pustoszyć Alfheim, oraz ślady spisku sięgającego głębiej, niż ktokolwiek przypuszczał.
W świecie, gdzie polityka, magia i dawne urazy mogą doprowadzić do wojny, Loki i Sigyn będą musieli zmierzyć się nie tylko z zagrożeniem ukrytym w cieniu lasu, ale także z uczuciem, którego od dawna nie potrafią nazwać.

summary:
Val heaves with a laugh and Loki welcomes his own. Ecstasy drowns them. It feels picturesque. His mind conjures a world wherein the amulet never leaves his neck, until it fuses into his skin, into his soul, sinking deeper and deeper until he and it are inextricable to a molecular level. Midday warms his face, snowmelt trickling, as Val speaks her well-wishes and eventual goodbye.
Loki waves her off and prances cheerfully down the street, stopped several times along the way by a bustle of, “I love your necklace!” and, “Wow, that’s a big emerald,” and, “Where’d you buy that?” and the occasional cry of, “Never take it off!” It feels as if reliving his olden days as King, wearing Odin’s face and serviced as pleased, worshiped not as a prince but as Allfather. It’s intoxicating.
—

Aurelia’s life in Asgard starts with Thor teaching her one very important palace skill: how to steal honey cakes from the kitchens without getting caught. What begins as harmless mischief quickly becomes a habit.
Between palace teasing, stolen sweets, royal expectations, and Asgard’s glittering chaos, Aurelia is pulled into the lives of two very different princes. Loki is clever, difficult, sharp-tongued, dramatic, and somehow even more impossible to ignore. (I decided it would be easier for me to have both versions, the Spanish one that I can easily read and the English one that I translate)
In a world where Metas — supernatural creatures — were hunted to the edge of extinction by humanity, two teenagers raised in Asgard discover that everything they knew was a lie.
Loki, prince of Asgard, never knew he was a frost giant slowly poisoned to appear human. Peter Parker, a common market boy, never knew he was a werewolf cub modified in a secret laboratory.
When the Avengers — warriors of the Meta Kingdom — tear them from their lives and deliver them to their biological parents, both boys face families who love them with suffocating intensity, cultures that see them as infants, and a war that needs them as weapons.
Laufey, King of the Metas, has recovered the baby stolen from him sixteen years ago. He will not let go again. Tony Stark and Steve Rogers have found the cub they thought was dead. They will not lose him twice.
But Loki is not a baby. Peter is not a cub. And neither of them asked to be saved.
Borders of blood separate two worlds. But blood also binds.
The Sons of War have awakened.

Laufey, el Rey de los Metas, ha recuperado al bebé que le robaron hace dieciséis años. No lo soltará de nuevo. Tony Stark y Steve Rogers han encontrado al cachorro que creían muerto. No lo perderán dos veces.
Pero Loki no es un bebé. Peter no es un cachorro. Y ninguno de los dos pidió ser salvado.
Las fronteras de sangre separan dos mundos. Pero la sangre también une.

title: El Susurro de las Estrellas
author: SoulAstral
summary:
La visión fue un estallido de agonía cósmica: doce estrellas destellando en colores imposibles antes de apagarse. Peter Parker comprendió demasiado tarde que el chasquido de Thanos había sido quirúrgico; no un genocidio aleatorio, sino una purga calculada. Iron Man, el Capitán América, Doctor Strange… los pilares de la resistencia, borrados de la existencia. El Titán Loco no solo ganó la guerra, sino que eliminó a quienes podían orquestar una contraofensiva.
La Tierra es un caos. Los héroes sobrevivientes, destrozados, se han rendido. No hay plan ni líder. Solo el.
Sin la magia de Strange o el mito de Rogers, Pero con la herencia de Stark. En la Torre de los Vengadores, ahora un mausoleo de tecnología silenciosa, el protocolo "Heredero de Hierro" le concede acceso total. Su obsesión no es la venganza, sino una ecuación imposible: revertir un chasquido sin gemas. Sabe que Thanos subestimó la variable definitiva: no al Hombre de Hierro, sino a la mente que él mismo vio capaz de superarlo. Peter Parker no es un reemplazo; es la evolución. El legado ya no es una armadura, sino la terquedad de un arácnido que tejerá, con los hilos de la derrota, una nueva realidad.

summary:
"How old were you when you were married to Thor?" Jane asks one day.
Sigyn's feels her lips purse. "Five and ninety." She says shortly. Shortly, but not curtly. Jane had said 'married to' Thor, not 'married' Thor. It's a two-letter difference, but it makes all the difference in the world to Sigyn. It acknowledges that there was little choice involved. 
This is why Jane is one of Sigyn's favourite Midgardians.
Jane pauses and visibly does the math. "You were sixteen?" Her voice is shrill.
"I suppose." Sigyn replies uncomfortably. 
"Why the fuck did they get away with that?" Jane demands. "I thought Asgardians came of age at a hundred."
Sigyn bites her tongue until the blood comes. "They do."
"Then what-"
"The Allfather made an exception." Sigyn looks down at her hands. "I wish to speak of something else."

Prince Loki of Asgard believes he is unworthy of Valhalla, a realm for honored warriors. There, he reflects on the fracture points that led to his divergence—living in Thor’s shadow, discovering his Jotun heritage, and the invasion of New York. Amelia has always seen herself as insignificant, the kind of bystander caught in the chaos of heroes and villains. But when the moment came where she really did become a mortal casualty, something changed. Survival morphed from luck to a responsibility. And now, Amelia was burdened with the purpose to prevent what was coming and to become someone with far more control than just an accidental victim in the world of heroes and villains.
What Amelia doesn’t realize is that some forces—and some people—cannot be controlled. And somewhere in the unraveling path ahead, a certain God of Mischief was already preparing to prove it.

Loki swallowed, and Gamora wondered if she had ever seen him so vulnerable. Not for a long time, she thought, not since he had first come to Sanctuary – when he’d been broken. Broken, just as she and Nebula had been.
“I have nowhere else.”
Gamora looked at him, and took account of every inch of the man before her. Gamora looked at him, and saw how he fidgeted. How he held his breath. How he hoped. Gamora looked at him, and recalled her conversation with Drax that morning.
“It is worth protecting, you know.”
“What is?”
“Family.”
Family.
She wanted hers whole.
Gamora looked at him – looked at her brother – and smiled.
“Welcome aboard, Loki.”
*****
What if Loki had never been sent to Earth by Thanos? What if he stayed on Sanctuary for years, a member of the Black Order alongside Nebula and Gamora until 2014, when he was sent with the sisters to aid Ronan's search for the Power Stone? Thor, sabe que el negocio pronto se recuperara, siempre sucede, no es poco lo que lleva teniendo la cafetería. Sin embargo, la adolescencia de su hijo no dura una temporada, sino años y superarla puede costarle la relación padre e hijo, por no saber cómo manejarlo, no tener la paciencia. La comunicación entre ellos se está perdiendo y solo puede ver como el alegre niño que una vez fue su hijo, se está convirtiendo cada día más en un adolescente apagado e infeliz.
La compañía y ayuda que Thor necesita, para con su hijo, puede venir en ropa de hombre y mujer. A su vez, la voz en la radio que suena en su cafetería, llegará al corazón de padre e hijo, llevándolos a comunicarse y comprenderse.

I closed my eyes, there were unshed tears there, I had drank too much, it had to be that. “Please, let me go.”
He laughed just the once, “Never I’m afraid, but I will take you to your rooms.”
Groaning “I already told Olaf or whoever it was that I didn’t want company to my rooms.”
“I’m not Olaf or whoever.” His voice was back to happy and eager. I couldn’t keep up with him.
“I still don’t need help.” Then why did I still let him escort me?
“And if those Sisters of yours aren’t in? If they’ve found other beds for the night? Who’s to get you out of your pretty dress.”
“Not you.” Part of me wanted to beg for it to be him.

December 2001 Midgard (Earth) New York, Queens Midgard also referred to as Earth, Terra had never been my favourite of the realms but on occasion I would find myself there. It was snowing hard when I walked past an orphanage and beheld the sight of a baby one the doorstep. It's irritating howls compelled me to knock on the door. It was freezing even a frost giant would be distracting by the cold, there was no answer the baby screamed louder surely someone would hear its screams. 14 minutes that was how long I stood with the child.
By Odin I had never known until that day that humans can be so ignorant. The baby is in a cardboard box, a thin blanket which had likely been put over it was now curled around one leg, if I was not mistaken by the smell it had relieved it yet it still craved more. title: Thor fell onto the beach one day
author: UnderwaterArch
summary:
Thor falls into another universe and is forced to kill another version of himself. Then he hears a song from the water, that he simply cannot resist.It was then (as he made a mental note never to use a narwhal horn as a decorative item) that he heard the song.
A hauntingly beautiful song; so sweet he felt he could open his mouth and have the melody melt on his tongue like spun sugar.
Surely it could only have come from the most talented singer in Valhalla, it so enchanted him.
It drew him towards the water, to the end of a long wooden dock. There, he found the source of the music and stopped short.
The singer rested his elbows on the end of the dock. The rest of his body dangling into the water and he had obviously just been swimming as his long black hair was dripping wet.
When the man saw him, he stopped singing, “You killed my brother,” he said.
“I-uh,” Thor stammered, “I’m sorry. It was an accident. I fell on this hut you see, and he attacked me-“
The man halted Thor’s apology with a wave of his hand. “No need to explain,” he said, “You’ve done me a great service. My name is Loki and I greet you warmly.”

Inspired by Loki's quote; "Sure. Burn it down, easy. Annihilating it, easy. Razing things to the ground is easy. Trying to fix what's broken is hard. Hope is hard."

summary:
Loki is rather used to sneaking about the palace grounds at night.
He's memorized the guard patrols down to the second and has learned how to fit into the rhythm of them as he ducks out of the royal chambers to the library to read books the librarian would never let him study in the light of day, or out to the gardens to experiment with his magic somewhere no one would think to find him, or even up to the observation tower to get a glimpse of the galaxies. There's a peace to Asgard in the middle of the night that allows him to breathe, to give voice to his most daring ideas as he wanders, a freedom that is painfully rare in the light of day.
But tonight, as he is darting past the training grounds, sticking to the tall hedges designed to block out sound from the greater grounds he hears a faint scuff of shoes. Curiously enough, the tread isn't heavy enough to be a soldier's boot and so Loki drifts a bit closer, rewarded with more shuffling and a few murmured curses in a voice that almost sounds familiar.

title: Evolved Devotion
author: KaptainArby
tags: Science Bros | Bruce Banner & Tony Stark Friendship
summary: To pray to a god is comparable to worship in its own right. The soul of the person engaged in prayer may call out to one god in particular, despite what the prayer entails or if it falls beneath the god’s dominion. Like finds like, after all.Loki, a trickster god, has never been the popular choice for prayers. Even at the height of worship, the prayers he received were few and far between, often coming from those that his godhood found resembled him. But when they were faced with him, rather than Thor or Frigga, they rescinded their prayer and refused his help, believing it would come at a cost to them. The truth of the matter was that Loki revered those that worshiped him, protecting and adoring them in kind, which made their rejections sting all the more. Nowadays, he was lucky if he received a single prayer within the span of a century.When he receives a prayer in the midst of a meeting with his father, brother, and the council of Asgard, he nearly collapses from the overwhelming emotion it elicits. summary: “Thor,” Odin said, waving a hand to dim the lights in the room as he rose to his feet. “Odinson. My heir. My firstborn. Long have you waited for this day, on which I bestow upon you the tasks of the konungsskapari. Before you is a map of the Nine, over which Asgard has ruled since Auðumbla licked Búri from the salt and rime of Ginnungagap. The Norns did not bestow such power upon our people lightly, and each would-be king of Asgard must prove himself worthy.“The heir is to complete nine tasks, one for each of the Nine Realms, and in doing so prove his worth.” Odin took the parchment in hand, turning it between his fingers for a moment before he continued. “Before I present you with your tasks, know this: the konungsskapari is not to be undertaken lightly. The quest is not designed to bring glory; rather, it is to shape the heir into the king both Asgard and the Nine are in need of. Once you leave, there is to be no turning back. title: The Broken Ones
author: iSneezeStars
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary: Sleep. Get up. Put on her armor. Face the day and smile. Smile. Smile! Come home and break down. This was the way Darcy Lewis lived her life. Her eyes opened and she sighed.“God damn it,” she slurred. She was awake and staring at her blurred ceiling. She had woken up again. Why? Why couldn’t she just not exist? Why couldn’t she have passed away in her sleep? At least then she wouldn’t have to pretend like there was a point to her life. She wouldn’t have to pretend like she mattered. She did the same thing every day, day in and day out. Wake up, get up, go to work, play babysitter, pretend she was fine, come home, cry and sleep. Then she would get up and do it all again. What point was there to her life? She wasn’t Jane; she wasn’t making scientific discoveries or trying to make the world a better place. She didn’t have someone to come home to at night, someone who loved her. She had nothing and no one… so what was the point of living?

"Why are you in my bed?!" Loki paid him no attention as he turned around, only showing Tony his backside as he put his leather back on and started strapping his armor back onto himself. If Tony didn't know better, he would have thought that Loki looked hurt, but Loki was crazy, bag full of cats crazy, and even if he was hurt, Tony shouldn't let that bother him. Then why was there a small part of him that did care? Loki didn't turn around until he had all of his armor back on, both literally and figuratively; his face was a stone.
"What are you doing here?!" Tony demanded. Loki looked at him, but his face gave nothing away. He walked past him like he was going to walk away, but Tony found his arm stopping him without realizing it.
"Why are you here? Why don't I remember?" Tony asked, but less angrily and more confused. Loki sighed again and turned around.
"This is not the first time this has happened," Tony frowned, then glared. That wasn't true; he sure as hell had never slept with Loki before, even if he had last night, which he still couldn't remember.

summary: No sopé de uma montanha islandesa, envolta por névoa e aurora boreal, duas deusas construíram um lar. Não um templo, nem um castelo — mas uma casa. Um espaço onde o silêncio tem presença, o verde resiste ao inverno, e cada cômodo carrega escolhas feitas com cuidado, longe do mundo.Hela, filha da morte, e Thena, filha da guerra, criaram um refúgio. Entre rituais, animais e o cotidiano sagrado, vivem um amor que não precisa ser dito. Juntas, celebram a pausa, o toque, o que permanece quando o mundo se cala.A casa respira com elas: constelações no teto, uma horta que floresce no gelo, uma estufa aquecida pelo improvável. O porão guarda memórias, o sótão, silêncio e arte. Cada canto pulsa com o que escolheram cultivar — e com o que decidiram deixar partir.Não é uma história de conquistas, mas de permanência. summary: Hela e Thena nunca precisaram de muito para se sentirem completas. Desde o primeiro olhar trocado — em meio a batalhas, ruínas e silêncios confortáveis —, souberam que o que tinham era raro demais para ser preenchido com expectativas alheias. Filhos? Era uma pergunta que não se encaixava no vocabulário delas. Nem tabu, nem desejo. Apenas uma ideia que não colava na pele, como um manto costurado para outras pessoas.Em vez de bercinhos e noites mal dormidas, escolheram taças de vinho, mapas antigos, o som grave de Garm se espreguiçando no tapete e o olhar altivo de Argus exigindo reverência. A família delas latia, miava, e existia com uma força silenciosa. Hela, deusa da morte, já sabia o que era ser mãe — ainda que em moldes divinos e disformes — e Thena, guerreira que amava com o corpo inteiro, nunca precisou parir para amar como se tivesse criado o mundo.Este é um retrato de quem escolheu o agora em vez do depois. De quem entendeu que nem todo amor precisa gerar continuidade — porque algumas histórias são tão cheias de vida que bastam em si mesmas. Uma ode à escolha, ao afeto sem moldes, e à liberdade de ser lar sem seguir roteiro.

summary: Thor shifted. Just a twitch. A small one. The kind of movement you made when your body dreamed of warmth and reached for it before your mind caught up. He mumbled something against his arm. summary: It started as a quiet session in the far garden, where Mother sometimes taught them seidr when the weather was good and the court was elsewhere. Nearby, the fountain’s steady trickle was the only sound besides the soft rustle of leaves stirred by a gentle breeze. Thor crouched across from Loki, both seated on worn stones, a shallow bowl of water between them to focus their magic. Loki’s illusion hovered neatly above his reflection: a falcon, wings shifting with the wind. Thor’s image was unstable, lightning flashing in the wrong places, the shape flickering and faltering.“Try again,” Loki said, voice tight with exasperation but softened by patience. “You’re thinking too loud again. Feel it. Less thunder, more thread.”“I am feeling it,” Thor snapped, running a hand through his damp hair, heat rising under his skin. The image collapsed with a hiss of steam. “It doesn’t stay.”Loki groaned, rising with a frustrated sigh. “You’re pushing it, not shaping it. It’s like trying to paint with a hammer.”“Maybe that’s all I have,” Thor muttered, voice low, breath uneven. “Maybe I’m not meant for this.”

“It’s been three days,” Loki says, as if Thor doesn’t know, as if he hasn’t been aching and pining for every second of every one of those days. “What have you been doing?”
“Tending to my duties. Hunting. Visiting our mother.”
“And then?”
“Then nothing.”
Loki leans in to press his lips against Thor’s neck in a trail of feathery kisses until he reaches Thor’s ear, where he bites down gently.
“I can smell her on you,” he says, whisper-soft and venomous.

He led them out of the great hall, and onto multiple, sweeping balconies that looked out from the palace. As they approached, he saw the two children look out into the sweeping city before them… the tall, golden towers that had held sturdy for eons. And the multicoloured Bifrost Bridge in the far distance, that led out over the storming sea of Ífingr and to the cosmos beyond the shimmering atmosphere of their home planet.
  He clapped a hand on both their shoulders. "I have great expectations of you both. You will both serve Asgard, not just for me… but for all of us."
  "Loki…" The black-haired boy grinned cheekily.
  "And Thor."
Thor Odinson, son of Odin — a fearsome, mighty warrior renowned amongst the gods of Asgard, a legend amongst mere mortals. He is destined to be king: but when a series of circumstances lead him to make some terrible choices, he will have to pay the price for putting his kingdom in jeopardy. summary:
Odin took Loki from her and stared down at the small infant. His son would grow up to serve a very important purpose someday. One that would greatly benefit Asgard and Jotunheim.
 
  A lasting peace between their people. There would be no need for the harsher and more costly methods of conquering in order to bring the Jotunn to heel. No more lives lost on either side. The Frost Giants would be under the leadership of one of their own people, but who would have unquestioning loyalty to Asgard and would ensure that they caused no future harm to any of the Nine Realms.
 
  Finding Loki in that temple was clearly meant for a much greater purpose than merely adopting a child. He was meant for this. That is what the future held. A throne for each of his sons. For the good of Asgard.
 In which Odin did not eventually set aside his plans for his adopted son. His love for the child is not enough to sway him from his plans. He is a better king than a parent. The child will serve an important purpose someday and must be ready for it. And Loki finds it even more difficult to grow up under the weight of these unknown expectations.

Odin fell into the Odinsleep to moment things got uncomfortable. Frigga, his mother and one of the only people he truly trusted, lied to him his entire life. And Thor was gone, banished, at the time Loki needed him most.And the worst part was that all of it felt like Loki's fault. Now here he was, King of Asgard, on the brink of war for the first time in centuries and he didn't know what to do or even who to trust.But at least that was familiar. He'd figure it out, alone, like he'd always done. title: What Matters in the End
author: Trygvasson
tags: Loki is short for a giant
summary: It had been centuries since Thor had last seen Loki. Six of them, he thought. For the first twenty years or so, he had assumed with utter certainty Loki had once more faked his own death and would show up again to drive him crazy soon enough. After thirty years with not only no contact but even no word, Thor began to doubt. After fifty years, he began to grieve. After a hundred years, he was done grieving. He had been living amongst humans for so long at that point, loss no longer felt unnatural. He treasured memories of the people he used to know; he was not worn down by them. There was too much else to keep him going. Now, New Asgard was thriving and growing. The Aesir accounted for 0.1% of Norway's population. Thor still regularly joined in adventures both on Midgard and off-world, although the Avengers was of course comprised of entirely new faces. Almost. The Hulk had proved to be immortal. They had also been joined by a handful of humans with bizarre genetic mutations that made them effectively immortal as well, so there was some constancy.Life was good.And then Loki showed up again. And there was something very wrong with him.

“This— This is incredible!” Mobius exclaims, and catches a flicker of surprise crossing Loki’s features.
  Loki.
Even he seems different— livelier, brighter, warmer. His dark hair isn’t pinned back, but combed, neat and soft; his face isn’t drawn, pale, and lifeless, but young, flushed, and exuberant. His eyes sparkle with something playful and mischievous; his lips are curled up, finally showing Mobius a true, full smile; his clothes are even straighter, neater, cleaner, more colorful, and Mobius takes him in, feeling like he is truly seeing Loki for the first time, like the Loki he saw before was merely a fading after-image.“Wow,” Mobius breathes, unable to fully believe this. “Loki, this— This is spectacular!”Loki hesitates, then asks, pretty mouth hypnotizing Mobius, “Aren’t you afraid?”“Afraid?” Mobius asks, bewildered.

Dreams plagued her tonight just like any other. It was nothing new. The flashes of battles across the back of her eyelids were all familiar, yet she had failed to grow accustomed to them, even after two hundred years. The golden halls had blurred in her memory with time, but the emotions kept their raw quality. The echoing words of reassurance rang in her ears.
“It’ll be alright. Just- just remember the story. If worst comes to worst, I’ll take the blame.”
--
Living on Midguard was nothing like her childhood. Jett was alone, old, and crippled. Her mind had long since turned against her, her only comfort being her familiar Bear. So when a group of, comparatively odd, mortals showed up at her door one fall morning, she initially thought they were just a hallucination. Turns out they weren't, and her peaceful life had officially slipped down the slope into chaos.

title: A Thousand Lives
author: GaryTheFish

summary: A year and a half has passed since Loki was brought to Midgard, a year and a half since Odin stripped him of his magic and immortality and banished him to Earth. Much to Odin's dismay, a very damaged Loki has embraced his sentence; defiant as always, he's done everything but throw it back in Odin's face. He's fought and bled for the realm onto which Odin cast him. He's built his own family. He's got a flat in London. He works for one of the most powerful men on Earth. He creates art - books to make the very angels weep, and on top of it all, he's in the midst of planning a wedding to a woman he loves more than anything. She may have even felt as though they were insulting her.For all Thor knew, maybe it would be a compliment that the two siblings she’d birthed had only found such pleasure in each other.

warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary: Loki was stunning. Truly. And Thor had no qualms admitting it. To himself. When he was alone. If Loki ever asked how a certain trinket or piece of cloth looked draped on him or hanging from his body, Thor would simply grunt and shrug, careful not to look too hard. He usually claimed that everything looked the same on his brother, and who was Loki trying to impress with such—well. Delicate and scant, clothing?That was generally responded to with a sigh and an eyeroll as though Thor were simply the daftest person Loki had ever met, and how dare he waste even a second of his attention.Thor would never admit that gold simply melted from Loki’s pale skin, and green made his eyes almost flare with life. And that when his hair was long and braided into plaits at the nape of his neck, Thor very much wanted to tug them free so that those thick, dark, almost-curls, could fall over his shoulders and make him look more the crown prince than Thor had ever been.Which… okay. Was maybe crossing the line into obsessive and inappropriate, but Thor just knew, deep inside, that he was looking out for his brother’s wellbeing. It was creepy. It was kind.

relationships: Lan Zhan | Lan Wangji/Wei Ying | Wei Wuxian
summary: Ghost Valley was peaceful, Loki thought as he absentmindedly watched the blooming forest in the distance, and one of the most beautiful places he had seen in his life. His book laid forgotten in his lap as he was mesmerized by the light of down sparkling over the trees.He had been desperate in the wake of the Battle of New York, had known that if Thor took him to Asgard he would not be allowed to defend himself. If he were allowed to speak at all, that was. He shuddered to think of what the Shield would have done had they gotten their hands on him and he would rather die than end up in Thanos' clutches again. His chances of a fair trial and potential freedom had been very low and he had known that were he to run one of his enemies would have eventually caught up to him. There had been only one place he could think of that would give him a chance, a place known to take in runaways and outlaws. Not criminals, at least not in his opinion, and that made all the difference. A place the Shield and Thanos would suspect not to look for him and Odin would dare not anger, not even to get to him.

tags: It's kid loki set during Thor 1
summary: The Avengers find themselves ensnared in a web of deception and self-discovery as Loki, the elusive God of Mischief, resurfaces with a startling revelation that challenges their beliefs. With fractured trust and conflicting emotions, the team embarks on a treacherous journey toward redemption, healing Loki's physical wounds and confronting the harsh judgment of Asgard's court. Bound by shared destiny and driven by a desire for justice, they become unexpected allies, defending Loki's innocence and championing his redemption.As Loki's fragmented memories resurface and the horrors of his past are unveiled, the Avengers and Loki forge an unlikely bond, defying the boundaries of fate and embarking on a transformative odyssey. Amidst the echoes of the past, they stand as beacons of hope, armed with empathy and the unwavering belief in second chances, reminding us that even the darkest shadows can be illuminated by the light of compassion and forgiveness in this epic tale of resilience, family, and the enduring power of redemption.
